# lab-secret-store

A sops file, a set of environment variables, or a vault, as something a floe can resolve.

<!-- Generated by nix build .#referencePages -->

## Inputs

| input | type | default | description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| backend | one of "sops", "env", "vault", "external" | `"sops"` | Where this store's keys live.  `sops`: an encrypted file at `secrets/<lab>/<store>.enc.yaml`. `env`: one environment variable per key, named `CATA_SECRET_<STORE>__<SECRET>__<KEY>` — uppercased, with every character that is not a letter or digit replaced by an underscore. The name is derived, so there is nothing to declare and nothing to keep in sync. `vault`, `external`: held somewhere outside catallaxy.  |
| removerCommand | null or (list of string) | `null` | How to remove a value from this store, for when the thing that produced it is destroyed.  Same contract as `writerCommand` minus the value: it receives `CATA_SECRET_KEY` and must exit non-zero if the key is still there. A store with no remover is not an error — destroying a stack says what it could not take back rather than refusing to finish.  |
| vaultPath | string | `"secret"` | KV mount path. |
| vaultServer | null or string | `null` | Base URL of the vault-compatible server, for a `vault` backend.  What `cata` dials from the *host*, so a routed name and not an in-cluster address. A cluster's own `VAULT_SERVER` answers the latter and is no use here, which is why nothing fills this automatically.  |
| vaultVersion | one of "v1", "v2" | `"v2"` | KV engine version.  An enum here though the CLI parses it as a plain string, because writing a v2 mount as though it were v1 succeeds and stores the wrong shape — which nothing notices until a reader gets an envelope where it expected a value.  |
| writerCommand | null or (list of string) | `null` | How to write a value into this store.  It receives `CATA_SECRET_KEY` in the environment and the value on stdin, and must exit non-zero if the write did not happen. Nothing is passed on the command line, so a value never reaches a process listing. This is what makes the set of backends open.  |

## Provides

| provision | signature | what it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| labStore | [LAB_SECRET_STORE](../signatures/LAB_SECRET_STORE.md) | A store on the operator's machine that `cata` reads authored secret values from. |

## What it emits

Rendered by `every-floe` as the lab unit `authored`. A unit of the lab
installs nothing into a cluster, and its provisions are sealed inside the
lab's inclusion — so its declaration above is its interface.
